method: Primary author paper, RFC Editor documents, and official project/template documentation. No secondary source is used for technical claims.

references.title: Exploring the Internet from space with Hypatia
references.use: Packet-level LEO simulation, predictable route changes, route-shortening reordering and false loss inference are prior observations.

references.title: CUBIC for Fast and Long-Distance Networks
references.use: CUBIC relevance and standardized congestion-control design; not equivalence of the course recovery stack to all current Linux implementations.

references.title: Improving the Robustness of TCP to Non-Congestion Events
references.use: Prior loss-decision delay and Extended Limited Transmit; the prototype does not implement TCP-NCR wholesale.

references.title: The RACK-TLP Loss Detection Algorithm for TCP
references.use: Prior transmission-time evidence and probing; no RACK-TLP implementation or Linux performance comparison is claimed.

references.title: Proportional Rate Reduction for TCP
references.use: Native recovery transmission accounting is preserved.

references.title: A Conservative Loss Recovery Algorithm Based on Selective Acknowledgment (SACK) for TCP
references.use: Packet-count presumed-loss evidence and SACK recovery background.

references.title: Controlled Delay Active Queue Management
references.use: CoDel's existing sojourn-time AQM mechanism; tested fixed defaults do not establish general CoDel inferiority.

references.title: TCP models and TcpSocketState pacing attributes
references.qualification: Model-library opening failed during reference verification; primary search text and official class attributes were inspected. The pinned course source controls actual evaluated behavior.

template.compiled_class: IEEEtran 1.8b conference, 10 point, US letter, unchanged default margins

claims_excluded: The reordering phenomenon is newly discovered.
The final segment allowance implements RACK-TLP or TCP-NCR.
The course ns-3 stack represents every modern TCP implementation.
The known-capacity pacing comparison establishes independent stock-plus-pacing gains or deployment-wide safety.
